verdicts.evidence: I reproduced this on a fresh site (API 8440, site 4440, database candela_v8440). Setup: the sealed circle 'The Ninth Night', reports open, and Ada files a report with a key over the WebSocket. Lightkeeper device A (1440x900) ticks one question: the paper shows TOTAL +3, ADD 3 ILLUMINATION. A presses Add and the database reads illumination 3. The log says 'The Ninth Night gains 3 Illumination (0 to 3).' and then 'milestone 3 reached!'. A shows 'Added 3 Illumination'. Device B is a separate browser context for the same Lightkeeper. It shows the track at 3 / 12 and a live 'ADD 2 ILLUMINATION' with TOTAL +2: the keys are counted again and the question ticks are blank. B presses Add, the database reads 5 and B shows 'Added 2 Illumination'. Screenshots: out_8440/tally_01_deviceA_added.png, tally_02_deviceB_fresh_live_add.png and tally_03_deviceB_added_again.png. A third fresh desk, opened later for another check, again showed a live 'ADD 2 ILLUMINATION' (out_8440/illum_01_manual_edit_log.png). This matches the regress seat's two-tab case (0 -> 2 -> 5). FAQ.md:224 says the tally is added 'with one press ... once per assignment', so this is not intended. It is also not one of the known limitations: those cover Notebook drafts, not the tally.
verdicts.root_cause: frontend/src/components/gm/CirclePage.jsx:309-316 reads the 'added' flag and the question answers from illumTallies[circId]. addTally (313-316) refuses a second add only when that browser's own copy says added. frontend/src/store/gameStore.js:1608-1613: setIllumTally only writes to the local store. No WebSocket message is sent for the ticks or the added flag. gameStore.js:2144 persists illumTallies to localStorage. The server gets only update_circle {illumination: illum + total} (backend/vtt/ws/handlers/gm.py:383-412). That is an absolute value with no tally context, so it cannot refuse a second add. As a result every other tab or device starts with added=null and blank answers, and any later add counts the keys again.
verdicts.fix: Keep the tally on the circle next to the assignment number. Store backstory_answers['tally'] = {answers:[bool,bool,bool], added:int|null} (backend/vtt/assignment.py). clear_paperwork pops it at End Assignment. Add two GM WebSocket messages: gm_set_tally_answers, refused once added, and gm_add_tally. gm_add_tally locks the circle row with with_for_update and refuses with 409 if tally.added is already set. Otherwise it computes the total server-side from the filed reports and the stored answers (port tallyReports), adds that total to illumination, stores added, and logs as handle_update_circle does. Send the tally in the circle dict to the GM's desk. CirclePage then reads circle.backstory_answers.tally instead of illumTallies. Remove illumTallies from the store and from partialize (gameStore.js:463, 1608-1613, 2144).

refute.reasoning:
The defect is real and the root cause is right. I read the code myself. In frontend/src/components/gm/CirclePage.jsx:309-316, the 'added' guard and the question answers come only from illumTallies[circId]. setIllumTally (gameStore.js:1608-1613) writes only to the local store, which is persisted to localStorage (gameStore.js:2144). handle_update_circle (backend/vtt/ws/handlers/gm.py:383-412) just applies an absolute illumination value and has no idea of a tally. So any other tab or device starts with added=null and blank ticks and can add the keys again. The regress seat saw 0 -> 2 -> 5 and the verifier saw 0 -> 3 -> 5 on a fresh site, which matches. FAQ.md:224 promises 'one press ... once per assignment'. Neither QUIRKS.md nor the known-limitations list covers the tally (the localStorage item there is about Notebook drafts), so this is not intended. No rulebook argument applies, because the book's rule is about the amount, not the UI. The fix is sound: the tally goes in backstory_answers next to the assignment number, clear_paperwork (assignment.py:47) is already where per-assignment paperwork gets popped, and a server-side gm_add_tally under a row lock that refuses a second add closes it properly.

The case against holds only on severity, which triage raised from medium (F010) to high. Every route needs the same Lightkeeper to press Add a second time on a second device or a second tab (and a second tab first needs 'Use this tab'). By then the track already shows the raised value, and the log already has 'gains N Illumination (x to y)' and the milestone line. The extra amount is limited to the keys (+2 or +4), because the question ticks come up blank. It is fully recoverable, since the Lightkeeper can edit the track directly. 'Early advancement' still needs the track to reach 12 and a deliberate Advance. The losing of question ticks across devices (F105) is low on its own. This is a real correctness gap against a documented promise, but it takes a human double-press with visible evidence that the tally was already added, and it can be undone. So medium, not high.

verdicts.evidence: Fresh site; spending is open (resources_editable) with a pool of 5/5/5. Bram Holt spends 1 Refresh over his socket (resources_spent_assignment=1, Refresh 4). Bram dies (is_dead, scars 4). Bram's user forges 'Tobias Reyes' and calls POST /campaign/rejoin, which needs no approval. Rows afterwards: Bram Holt spent 1, retired; Tobias Reyes spent 0, active. The phone desk at 390x844 for Tobias shows 'YOUR SPENDS 0 / 2' with every Spend button live (out_8440/spend_01_tobias_fresh_count.png). The same paper's printed rule reads 'Each player may spend up to two between assignments.' Tobias then spends Stitch and Train, both accepted (Tobias spent 2), and a third spend is refused. Final pool is 4/4/4: one player took 3 resources out of the pool in one break. FAQ.md:263 says 'each player has two per assignment'. I rate it low, not medium, for three reasons: it needs a death between assignments, the dead investigator's own spend does nothing more for the player, and the Lightkeeper can give a spend back or refill the pool.
verdicts.root_cause: The counter lives on the character, not on the player. backend/vtt/ws/handlers/circle.py:72 checks character.resources_spent_assignment >= 2 and line 96 increments it on the character. Neither backend/vtt/routers/campaigns.py:278-355 (rejoin) nor the invite-rejoin path carries the count from the retired investigator (retired at campaigns.py:333-334). The new character starts at the model default 0 (models.py:267). The frontend shows that per-character value (frontend/src/components/pc/CircleView.jsx:812).
verdicts.fix: Smallest fix, in rejoin() at backend/vtt/routers/campaigns.py:333: before retiring old_chars, set new_char.resources_spent_assignment = max([new_char.resources_spent_assignment or 0] + [c.resources_spent_assignment or 0 for c in old_chars]). This is safe across assignments. A dead investigator keeps status 'active' until it is replaced, so End Assignment (gm.py:323) already reset its count, and only spends from the current break carry over. Add a test: spend 1, die, rejoin, then expect 1/2 and refusal after one more spend.

refute.reasoning:
The finding stands at low severity, not the cluster's medium. I read the code instead of reproducing, because the verifier's repro and the playtest database already agree with it.

**What the code does.** The limit is stored on the character. `handle_spend_resource` in `backend/vtt/ws/handlers/circle.py` checks and increments `character.resources_spent_assignment` (lines 72 and 96). `rejoin()` in `backend/vtt/routers/campaigns.py` (lines 278-355) retires the old characters (line 334) and carries nothing over. The new character starts at 0 (`models.py:267`).

**What the playtest showed.** In `candela_playtest`, Bram Okafor is retired, dead, spent=1. Tobias Okafor-Reyes, owned by the same user, is active with spent=0. bram's notes record "spends 0/2 fresh".

**The strongest case against it, and why it fails.**
- *A new investigator is a new PC, and the resource effects are per PC* ("Refresh ... for one PC"), so a fresh character could reasonably get its own spends. The rulebook does not cover a replacement in the middle of a break. But the site states the rule per player in three places:
  - the printed circle-sheet rule (`frontend/src/game/circleResources.js:23-24`): "Each player may spend up to two between assignments";
  - `FAQ.md:263`: "each player has two per assignment";
  - `docs/refactor/RULES_CHECK.md` item 16, which quotes p. 41 as "Each player may spend up to two" and cites the p. 62 example as counting spends per player.

  So the site contradicts its own stated rule. That is not intended behaviour.
- **Harness artifact?** No. The rejoin path is the normal death-replacement flow. It needs no GM approval, and it was used in the real playtest.
- **Unrealistic setup?** Partly. It needs a death while spending is open and the count has not been reset. In the playtest the Lightkeeper left spending open after End Assignment, and the death came during the next assignment's play. The cluster's "death mid-break" is a slightly narrow description of the trigger.

**Why low.**
- The practical gain is small. A freshly forged investigator has no marks and full drives, so Stitch and Refresh do nothing for it at join time. Train (an extra die) is the only immediate gain, unless spending stays open into play.
- The dead investigator's spend is wasted anyway.
- The Lightkeeper can correct it with "Give a spend back" (`gm.py:431`) or by editing the pool.

**The fix is right.** Carrying the max of the old characters' counts into `new_char` in `rejoin()`, before they are retired, covers both the invite path and the death-rejoin path, because both go through this one function. It is safe across assignments: `gm_end_assignment` (`gm.py:323`) resets every status-active character, and dead characters stay active until replaced, so only the current period's spends carry over.

**Two gaps in the fix.**
- A character retired earlier in the same break is not in `old_chars` (that query filters on active or dead), so its spends would not carry.
- A GM-approved ordinary join with a new character does not carry the count either. That is arguably the Lightkeeper's call.

The proposed regression test is right: spend 1, die, rejoin, expect 1/2, then refusal after one more spend.

verdicts.evidence: Fresh site, laptop at 1366x768. Over the API, Dev proposes Rival to Cass ('Dev: she reads gravel...') and Cass proposes Rival to Dev ('Cass: he is always a step behind.'). Cass then accepts Dev's. The relationships table holds row 8 (Cass->Dev, Rival, proposed) and row 9 (Dev->Cass, Rival, accepted). Cass's Circle tab (out_8440/rel_01_cass_crossing.png) shows two headed sections. 'YOUR RELATIONSHIP TO DEV OKAFOR' holds Rival with her own words, 'Waiting for Dev Okafor' and Edit. 'DEV OKAFOR'S RELATIONSHIP TO YOU' holds Rival with his words and 'Confirmed by you both'. That matches what Cass saw in the playtest (shots/cass/116_c2.png), where the two cards also carry different words. The site deliberately models relationships as directional, one per direction, each with its own type and answer and each confirmed by the other party. The component's two slots show this: frontend/src/components/pc/relationships/RelationshipNegotiation.jsx:194-195 (mine / theirs) with separate headings at 222 and 243. The formation papers count them the same way (DESIGN.md:412, 'confirmed out of proposed'). Her proposal is not a copy of his: it holds her own answer, and dropping it on accept would lose what she wrote. What the playtest saw is the site working as designed, not a duplicate.
verdicts.root_cause: Not a defect. backend/vtt/ws/handlers/circle.py:201-231 (propose) and 234-258 (respond) treat (from, to) and (to, from) as separate rows by design. RelationshipNegotiation.jsx shows them as 'Your relationship to X' and 'X's relationship to you'.
verdicts.fix: No fix needed. If the product wants one relationship per pair, that is a product decision and a model change, not a bug fix. A small optional UX touch: when the crossing proposal has the same type, have the waiting card say 'Dev also has a Rival relationship to you (confirmed)'.

verdicts.evidence: Fresh site, Lightkeeper at 1440x900, illumination at 5 after a tally add. I clicked a higher pip on the track. Illumination became 8 and the log read 'The Ninth Night gains 3 Illumination (5 to 8).' then 'The Ninth Night milestone 6 reached!' (out_8440/illum_01_manual_edit_log.png, desk note 'milestone 6 reached!'). The tally's Add press logs the same wording ('gains 3 Illumination (0 to 3)'). So the behaviour reproduces, but FAQ.md:224 documents it: 'Every change to the track is logged, such as "The Ninth Night gains 2 Illumination (3 to 5)."' Only the Lightkeeper can change the track (handle_update_circle returns when the socket is not the GM's), so the line is accurate: the track did gain 7 from 5 to 12. The finding itself says allowing the edit is fine and that Ada found the rest of the bookkeeping correct. Asking for different wording is a wish, not a defect.
verdicts.root_cause: backend/vtt/ws/handlers/gm.py:383-412 (handle_update_circle) logs every illumination change with the same 'gains N Illumination (a to b)' line (line 409). The tally's Add (frontend/src/components/gm/CirclePage.jsx:313-320) and a pip click send the same update_circle message, so the server cannot tell them apart. This is the documented behaviour in FAQ.md:224.
verdicts.fix: None required. If the product wants the source shown (a product decision), the cleanest route is the fix for illumination-tally-added-twice: a separate gm_add_tally message would log 'gains N Illumination from the assignment reports (a to b)', and update_circle could then log 'The Lightkeeper set Illumination to b (was a).'

verdicts.evidence: Fresh copy (API 8441, site 4441, DB candela_v8441). Four players and a Lightkeeper, sealed in SQL. Bram had 3 scars and Body 3. The Lightkeeper dealt Body with From an enemy unchecked, and Bram recorded the fourth scar on a 390x844 phone. DB: scars_count 4, is_dead t. After 'Stay and look at the sheet' (out_8441/b06_bram_dead_sheet.png), all 9 roll rows had aria-disabled=false, and the 3 Take mark buttons and Change gear were still live. Pressing Roll Focus went through. Ada's desk received an activity_log line for Bram's roll, and the LK desk logged 'Bram Okafor rolled Focus, a 5: Mixed success' (b07_bram_dead_roll.png, b10_lk_dead_sheet.png). Bram's Circle page showed 'Spend 1 Stitch/Refresh/Train', all enabled. With circles.resources_editable=true and refresh=1, a spend_resource from the dead man's socket was accepted: refresh went 1 -> 0, nerve was restored, and the table logged 'Bram Okafor used Refresh'. So a dead investigator can take the circle's last shared resource. take_mark on the dead socket was also processed (it opened a Death Defy offer). The Lightkeeper's copy of the dead sheet still offers Deal a mark. FAQ.md:139 documents that the server enforces nothing beyond the flags, but it says the frontend 'reflects the dead state', and the sheet already disables ability Use for the dead (InvestigatorDossier.jsx:188). Locking rolls, marks and spends was clearly intended and was missed. Severity is lowered to medium: the player has to choose to stay on the sheet and act.
verdicts.root_cause: Nothing checks is_dead. Frontend: InvestigatorDossier.jsx:1104 `const rollBlocked = !!pendingGildedChoice || !!isRolling;` ignores character.is_dead, and the same goes for the mark boxes (holdMark, around :1294), the drive +/- and Change gear. CircleView.jsx:~899 renders the Spend 1 buttons without checking the player's own death. Server: vtt/ws/access.py check_message (:449-458) has no is_dead rule. vtt/ws/handlers/circle.py:65 handle_spend_resource and rolls.py:329 handle_roll act for a dead character.
verdicts.fix: Server: in access.check_message, add `if not ctx.is_gm and character is not None and character.is_dead and action in DEAD_REFUSED: refuse 409 'Bram Okafor is dead: the sheet is a record.'`. DEAD_REFUSED = roll, resolve_gilded, use_post_roll_ability, burn_resistance, take_mark, resolve_ability_mark, intercept_mark, spend_resource, update_drive, update_gear, apply_advancement, use_ability, circle_relationship_propose. Also refuse a GM take_mark on a dead character. Frontend: in InvestigatorDossier, add `|| !!character?.is_dead` to rollBlocked (:1104), and treat is_dead like readOnly for the mark boxes, drive controls and Change gear. Keep 'Create a new investigator'. In CircleView, disable the Spend buttons when the player's own character is dead. GMCharacterSheet should hide Deal a mark when sheet.is_dead. Update the FAQ.md:139 wording.

verdicts.evidence: Same run: Bram recorded his fourth scar on the phone. WebSocket frames received after the scar: LK ['member_update'], Ada ['member_status'], Dev ['member_status'], Bram ['character_update','member_status']. No activity_log reached anyone. Only Bram's phone showed 'Bram Okafor is deceased.', a line the browser makes for itself from its own character_update (b02_bram_death_modal.png). On the LK desk, Ada's desk (1920x1080) and Dev's tablet (820x1180), the newest line was still 'Bram Okafor has been incapacitated!'. Ada's Your Circle silently dropped Bram (out_8441/b04_ada_after_death.png). The Lightkeeper then removed the fourth scar, and LK, Ada and Dev all logged 'The Lightkeeper removed a scar from Bram Okafor's record (3 of 4). Bram Okafor is alive, and incapacitated until revived.', a take-back of a death no one but Bram had seen. FAQ.md and DESIGN.md do not say a death should stay private, and incapacitation is announced to everyone (marks.py:199), so the gap is real.
verdicts.root_cause: backend/vtt/ws/handlers/character.py:79-80 handle_apply_scar calls only announce_death on a new death. announce_death (handlers/circle.py:274-286) sends just member_status to the players, with the GM key excluded, and writes no activity_log. The only death line comes from frontend/src/store/gameStore.js:740-748 (becameDead from the owner's own character_update), so it appears on the dying player's desk alone.
verdicts.fix: In handle_apply_scar, after `if character.is_dead and not was_dead:`, broadcast_campaign an activity_log such as {message: f'{character.name} has died: a fourth scar.', log_type: 'danger', ink_color: character.ink_color} to the whole campaign, the GM included. Use the existing _log pattern from marks.py. In gameStore.js:740-748, stop adding the local 'is deceased.' line for becameDead (keep the incapacitated one if needed) so the dying player does not see it twice.

verdicts.evidence: Lightkeeper at 1440x900, Bram with Body 3 (drained and reset first). Deal a mark > Body, not from an enemy. The LK sheet showed Body/Brain/Bleed empty, INCAPACITATED, 0 / 4. Nothing said a scar was waiting, and the Deal a mark buttons stayed enabled (out_8441/a03_lk_sheet_incap.png). Bram's phone had the scar form open. Bram recorded the scar: the LK sheet moved to 1 / 4 with the scar text, but no desk got a log line for the recorded scar (a05_lk_after_scar.png; the LK and Ada logs show nothing between 'has been incapacitated!' and the next deal). The LK has no way to tell that a scar is still owed. Not a defect: four Bleed marks dealt to the still-incapacitated Bram logged 'took a fourth Bleed mark.' and then 'has been incapacitated!' again. That fourth mark really is a second scar (rulebook p.14), and the DB showed incapacitated t with a new scar form, so the repeat is accurate. Also not a defect: the expectation that the 4th mark stays on show until the scar is written contradicts the rule the site implements, where the overfilled track clears when the scar is taken (RULES_CHECK.md item 9, marks.py:193). Confirmed parts: no pending-scar state on the Lightkeeper's sheet, and no log line for a recorded scar.
verdicts.root_cause: The pending scar lives only in server memory, in awaiting_scar (backend/vtt/ws/handlers/marks.py:75). trigger_scar goes to the character's channel only (marks.py:197), and get_char_dict (vtt/serializers.py, around :72) has no pending flag, so the GM's sheet (member_update) cannot show one. backend/vtt/ws/handlers/character.py:47-90 handle_apply_scar broadcasts character_update and nothing to the activity log, except the Not Again / Forbidden Ritual lines.
verdicts.fix: (1) In handle_apply_scar, broadcast_campaign an activity_log such as f'{name} recorded a scar ({n} of 4).' (skip it when the scar kills, since the death line covers that). (2) Add 'scar_pending': character.id in awaiting_scar to get_char_dict, so member_update carries it. In InvestigatorDossier's status stamp (:1312-1318), show 'Incapacitated: scar to record' when it is set. Optional wording tweak at marks.py:199: when the character was already incapacitated, log 'takes another scar' instead of 'has been incapacitated!'.

verdicts.evidence: After Bram recorded a scar, his phone had a Revive button (count 1) and the LK copy of the sheet had none (count 0) (out_8441/a05_lk_after_scar.png). After the Lightkeeper lifted a death by removing the fourth scar, the log said 'incapacitated until revived', yet the LK sheet still had no Revive. FAQ.md:129 says 'a GM can revive the character', and FAQ.md:139 says 'A GM can still manually issue revive_character'. The server accepts a GM-targeted revive: from the LK campaign socket, revive_character {character_id} set incapacitated f and logged 'Bram Okafor has been revived and is operational.' (v8441_d.js). The same test turned up a second bug that a UI-only fix would leave in place: on a GM-sent revive, the player's own channel got only the activity_log and no character_update (v8441_e.js: player frames ['activity_log']; the GM channel got character_update plus member_update). The player's desk would keep showing Incapacitated until a reload.
verdicts.root_cause: frontend/src/components/pc/InvestigatorDossier.jsx:1327 shows Revive only when `!readOnly`, and GMCharacterSheet.jsx:213 renders the sheet readOnly with traumaEdit = {setMarks, setScars, dealMark}, with no revive. gameStore.js:1486-1490 reviveCharacter sends no character_id, so it can only revive the socket's own character. backend/vtt/ws/handlers/character.py:100 handle_revive_character broadcasts character_update to ctx.channel, which is the GM's campaign channel when the GM sends it, not character_key(character.id) as gm.py:168 does.
verdicts.fix: Add a store action gmRevive(characterId) that sends {type:'revive_character', payload:{character_id}}. Pass revive in traumaEdit from GMCharacterSheet, and in the dossier render a Revive button beside the stamp when traumaEdit?.revive && character.incapacitated && !character.is_dead. In character.py:100, broadcast to character_key(character.id) instead of channel; the manager's SHEET_IN path then still sends member_update to the GM. Optionally refuse a revive of a dead character, as WEBSOCKET.md:82 already documents.

verdicts.evidence: Fresh site on 8442/4442, database candela_v8442 (dropped afterwards). Sealed campaign 'The Main Watch' had bram_v78ju's Bram Okafor active and alive (0 scars). Lightkeeper at 1440x900 used Roster > Invite player, typed bram_v78ju and pressed Send invite. The slip read only 'The player rejoins with a new investigator, without waiting for your approval. ... Invite sent to bram_v78ju.' and named no current investigator (out_8442/inv_02_slip_sent.png). The GM socket received no frames, so there was no log line. The DB now had pending_rejoin_campaign_id=1 while Bram Okafor was still active. On Bram's living desk (390x844 phone) the banner read 'Your Lightkeeper invites you back to The Main Watch with a new investigator.' with Create investigator, and gave no warning (inv_03_bram_desk_banner.png). The banner is deliberately shown on a living desk: MainDeskView.jsx:306 `rejoinInvite && !character?.is_dead`. Accepting means POST /campaign/rejoin with a new unaffiliated character, the same call the creator's 'Save and rejoin' makes (AppRouter.jsx:107). After it, the DB showed 'Bram Okafor|retired|is_dead f' and 'Bram Second|active'. The GM got investigator_approved, character_joined_mid_campaign and circle_update, but no activity_log. The Activity Log still read 'Nothing logged yet', and Bram Okafor's card was simply replaced (inv_04). Bram's Registry after sign-in lists only Bram Second; the living Bram Okafor is gone (inv_06_bram_hub_registry.png). The creator's last step (CharacterCreator.jsx:1534-1546) asks only 'Rejoin it with this investigator?'. Not a harness artifact. It is not intended either: FAQ.md and DESIGN.md describe the invite as bringing a player 'back', and nothing documents that it retires a living investigator. The retire-on-rejoin itself is pinned on purpose (test_rejoin_retires_living_active_character_of_same_user), so what is wrong is that nothing says so.
verdicts.root_cause: backend/vtt/routers/campaigns.py:411-432 (invite_rejoin) only sets invitee.pending_rejoin_campaign_id. It never looks at the invitee's active, living character in this campaign, returns just {ok: True} and writes no log_line. rejoin() at campaigns.py:325-334 then sets every other active or dead character of that user in the campaign to 'retired'. No step tells either side: InvitePlayer.jsx:91 shows only 'Invite sent to <name>', and the player-side texts (MainDeskView.jsx:306-311, RejoinInviteBanner.jsx, CharacterCreator.jsx:1537) do not mention that the current investigator will be retired.
verdicts.fix: Smallest fix: in invite_rejoin, look up the invitee's living active character in this campaign (Character.campaign_id==campaign_id, user_id==invitee.id, status=='active', is_dead False). Return its name in the response ({ok, current_investigator: name|null}) and await log_line(db, campaign.campaign_code, campaign.id, f'The Lightkeeper invited {invitee.username} back.'). In InvitePlayer.jsx, when current_investigator is set, show 'Invite sent to X. Their investigator <name> will be retired when they rejoin.' On the player side, add one line to the creator's rejoin box (CharacterCreator.jsx:1537) and to the desk banner when the current character is alive and in that campaign: '<name> will be retired.' Whether the server should refuse an invite while a living investigator remains is a product decision.

verdicts.evidence: Fresh site, cass_v78ju on the hub at 1366x768 with Mina Vale active in 'Side Case'. The Lightkeeper pressed Retire campaign… and the armed hint read 'Press again to retire Side Case. Every investigator leaves it and no one can join. Nothing is deleted.' (out_8442/ret_02_gm_armed.png). Then Yes, retire campaign. The DB showed 'Mina Vale|retired|campaign_id 2' and 'Ivo Pell|retired|2'. After a fresh sign-in, Cass's Registry lists Cass Moreau, Tess Arden and Wren Hale only. Mina Vale shows in no section, neither free nor retired (ret_09_cass_ledger_reload.png). The Case Ledger aria reads '3 in play'. GET /api/investigators still returns Mina with status 'retired', so the hub alone hides her (only active, pending and unaffiliated are rendered). The server would even accept /campaign/join for her, which shows the restriction is only how she is displayed. This contradicts FAQ.md:167: 'retire ... detaches all active/pending characters (sets their campaign_id to null and status to unaffiliated)', and it is the opposite of delete, which releases them (deletion.py:150-170). The other half of the cluster, Side Case vanishing from the Lightkeeper's Ledger with no retired list, matches FAQ.md:167 ('Retired campaigns are excluded from the GM's campaign list but the data is not deleted'), so that part is by design.
verdicts.root_cause: backend/vtt/routers/campaigns.py:223-228 (retire_campaign) sets every active and pending character to status 'retired' and keeps campaign_id. The characterization test backend/tests/test_campaigns.py:373-376 pins this as-is. The hub's PlayerRegistryPage.jsx:43/70/100 and CaseLedgerTome.jsx:55 show only active, pending and unaffiliated characters, so a retired living investigator disappears. FAQ.md:167 documents the opposite, unaffiliated with no campaign.
verdicts.fix: In retire_campaign, release living characters as delete does: for each active or pending character with is_dead False, set status='unaffiliated', campaign_id=None, ink_color=''. Leave dead ones as 'retired'. Collect their ids before the commit and broadcast campaign_retired to their character_key channels as well (this also covers D3 for them). Update test_campaigns.py:373-376 to expect unaffiliated/None for living members. Name the investigators in the GM's armed hint (GMDeskHeader.jsx:14) only if wanted. A retired-campaigns list for the GM is a product decision; FAQ says they are hidden.

verdicts.evidence: Fresh site, unsealed campaign 'Open Doors'. cass_v78ju sent two join requests (Tess Arden, Wren Hale) and dev_v78ju sent one (Dev Marsh). verdicts.root_cause: The owner is never sent or shown. backend/vtt/serializers.py:28-100 get_char_dict has no user_id or username, and it feeds investigator_joined pending_investigators and the approval payloads. backend/vtt/schemas.py:391-405 CharacterRosterItem (GET /campaign/{id}/roster, built in campaigns.py get_roster) has no owner field. frontend/src/components/gm/PlayerRosterCard.jsx:28-33 renders only name, pronouns/role/specialty and catalyst. backend/engine.py:42-77 request_join_campaign and :79 approve_investigator do not look at other characters of the same user in the campaign.
verdicts.fix: Add the owner's username to the roster item: an owner_username field in CharacterRosterItem filled from c.user.username in get_roster's to_item, plus 'owner_username' in get_char_dict, so live investigator_joined frames carry it too. In PlayerRosterCard.jsx, print 'from <username>' in mono under the name. In CorrespondenceStack.jsx, flag a request whose owner_username matches another pending or active card ('<username> already has an investigator here'). Optionally, the hub can note a second pending request to the same campaign. Whether the server should refuse a second request from one player is a product decision.

verdicts.root_cause: backend/vtt/routers/campaigns.py:231-234 broadcasts campaign_retired after the characters are already 'retired', so only the GM channel gets it (WEBSOCKET.md D3). The hub also never re-reads the list. frontend/src/components/campaignSelector/useCampaignEntry.js:28 refetches on opening the book only when the lists are empty. usePendingApprovalWatch.js:37-43 polls only while something is pending. enterAsPlayer (useCampaignEntry.js:42-48) enters the desk from the cached row without re-checking status.
verdicts.fix: Smallest fix: in useCampaignEntry.handleOpenRoster, always call fetchUserData(accessSession.userId) when the book opens, not only when the lists are empty. Also refetch on visibilitychange in CampaignSelector, as the pending watch does. In enterAsPlayer, re-check the character's fresh status (refreshCharacterStatus) and show a hub notice instead of entering if it is no longer active. Server side, together with the retire fix, send campaign_retired with broadcast_users to the owners of the released characters (as restore_campaign does), and have the gameStore campaign_retired handler call fetchUserData and set a hubNotice like campaign_deleted (gameStore.js:1108-1125).

verdicts.root_cause: frontend/src/components/gm/SceneManager.jsx:147-149 keeps location, atmosphere and ownText in useState, seeded from circle.location, circle.atmosphere and circle.dispatch_text, which hold the last sent dispatch. frontend/src/components/gm/OperationsPanel.jsx:155-159 renders <SceneManager /> only while activeTab === 'roster', so switching to Map, Notebook or Circle unmounts it and the draft is lost. On remount the fields come back as the last sent dispatch, or empty if none was sent. Only the Own words/Template mode is saved (MODE_KEY in localStorage, SceneManager.jsx:131-137).
verdicts.fix: Smallest fix: keep the draft outside the component. Either (a) move location, atmosphere and ownText into the zustand store (for example a dispatchDraft slice) and clear it in broadcastScene on send, or (b) save them in localStorage under candela-dispatch-draft:<userId>:<campaignId>, as Notebook drafts and the mode are saved. Seed useState from the draft when there is one and fall back to the circle values otherwise. The sync effects at SceneManager.jsx:152-154 should then overwrite the draft only when the circle values change because a dispatch arrives, not on mount. Another option is to keep SceneManager mounted but hidden on other tabs, though that changes the layout more.

verdicts.root_cause: frontend/src/components/shared/TableStrip.jsx:17-55 renders the tension as text only. frontend/src/components/gm/OperationsPanel.jsx:152-154 puts it in the left column when a sheet is open, while the hourglass with its - and + (TensionSection / TensionClock in SceneManager.jsx) renders only in the roster view with no sheet open.
verdicts.fix: Needs a product decision: should the strip be interactive on the Lightkeeper's desk? If yes, the smallest change is a `controls` prop on TableStrip, passed only from OperationsPanel.jsx:153. With it the strip adds two small 'Lower tension by one' and 'Raise tension by one' buttons around the n/4. They would send the same socket message as TensionClock's handlers (reuse that function from SceneManager.jsx), clamped 0..4. The strip must then also draw at tension 0 when controls are on. verdicts.evidence: Fresh unsealed table 'The Open Papers', approved player on a tablet 820x1180 with touch (/home/user/pt2/verify/v8443_stray.js and v8443_stray2.js). The formation papers open as role=dialog aria-modal=true and cover x 26-794 and y 59-1121 (out_8443/s01_papers.png). The player desk's CIRCLE tab sits under the dialog at css y 246-290. elementFromPoint over that rect returns, from top to bottom, the 'I. CIRCLE QUESTION' header, the dialog body, then the visible Q1 card. A real Playwright touch on the dimmed backdrop outside the dialog (10,600) cast no vote and the dialog stayed open. A Playwright click on the CIRCLE tab is refused because it is covered (timeout). A raw touch at the lower part of the tab's rect (615,286) sent circle_creation_vote question q1, because that point is the visible Q1 card. /home/user/pt2/seat.js:145-155 shows how --tap works: it takes the target's bounding box and sends CDP Input.dispatchTouchEvent at its centre with no check that something covers it. That is exactly how Dev's 03:42:47 q1 vote landed. A person sees the papers and would tap the question card itself, so the site behaved correctly.
verdicts.root_cause: Harness: /home/user/pt2/seat.js:145-155 (--tap dispatches a raw CDP touch at a covered element's coordinates without an occlusion check), so the tap aimed at the Circle tab hit the Q1 vote card drawn over it in the modal formation papers. The site behaved correctly: the backdrop does not vote, and the modal blocks the tab.
verdicts.fix: No site change. In seat.js, before a --tap, check that document.elementFromPoint(x, y) is the target or inside it, and fail with 'covered by …' otherwise, as Playwright's own click does.

verdicts.evidence: Fresh copy (API 8444, site 4444, database candela_v8444), script /home/user/pt2/verify/v8444_end.js, Lightkeeper at 1440x900. verdicts.root_cause: backend/vtt/ws/handlers/gm.py:325 (handle_gm_end_assignment calls clear_paperwork, backend/vtt/assignment.py:47-53, which pops the reports and moves the assignment number on whether or not the tally was added). frontend/src/components/gm/SceneManager.jsx:343 (armedHint) and :221 (receipt) never mention reports. verdicts.fix: Smallest fix: in SceneManager.jsx, build the armedHint and receipt from the store. Always add 'The reports close and are cleared.' When reports are filed and illumTallies[circle.id] for assignmentOf(circle) has no 'added', add a warning such as 'N filed reports' Illumination (+X) has not been added and will be lost; add it on the Circle page first.' (reuse tallyReports from game/illumination.js). Optionally also put 'The reports close and are cleared' in the server log line at gm.py:343, which already says 'reset'. Adding the tally automatically, or carrying it over to the next assignment, would be a product decision.

verdicts.root_cause: Client: frontend/src/store/gameStore.js:600. connect() with keepLog=false (entering the desk from the hub: useCampaignEntry.js:44/61, MainDeskView.jsx:59) sets tableRoll: null. For the same desk, lastRoll is kept (line 608 clears it only for another desk). DiceVault.jsx:58 derives settled = !!tableRoll, so canResist (DiceVault.jsx:75) and postRollChoiceWaiting (gameStore.js:206) treat an already settled roll as open again. A 409 burn refusal (gameStore.js:847ff) does not settle it either. Server: handle_gm_end_assignment (backend/vtt/ws/handlers/gm.py:302-350) never clears rolls.py's in-memory _last_roll (rolls.py:228), so the last roller's burn (rolls.py:725) is accepted after the assignment has ended. The client also gets no signal to drop lastRoll when the assignment number changes (gameStore.js:758 clears only the reports).
verdicts.fix: 1) Server: in handle_gm_end_assignment, for each active character, pop _last_roll and _pending_gilded entries (add a small settle_campaign_rolls(campaign_id) helper in rolls.py, the same loop as _hold_or_throw lines 160-163) so a stale burn is refused. 2) Client: in the circle_update branch at gameStore.js:758, when assignmentOf changes, also set lastRoll: null, lastRollKept: null, pendingGildedChoice: null and NO_OFFERS. 3) Client: keep a roll settled across a same-desk reconnect, either by moving tableRoll: null from line 600 into the different-desk branch at line 608, or by storing a separate settledRollId that DiceVault reads in place of !!tableRoll. Also settle the offer (set a flag or clear lastRoll's offer) when action_rejected arrives for burn_resistance.

verdicts.root_cause: frontend/src/components/pc/dice/PassNotes.jsx:16-24. targetOptions maps every investigator, the sender included, to '@Name (private)' and has no '@Lightkeeper' option for a player. verdicts.fix: In PassNotes.jsx targetOptions: filter out the desk's own character (compare inv.id to useGameStore(s => s.character?.id) when !showGmControls). Add { value: '@Lightkeeper', label: '@Lightkeeper only' } for players. Label player-to-player private options '@Name (and the Lightkeeper)'. In chat.py:61, treat target.lower() == '@lightkeeper' as reserved (skip the character lookup) so a character named 'Lightkeeper' cannot receive it. verdicts.evidence: Script /home/user/pt2/verify/v8444_phone.js, phone with touch. A New Scar (Dev, 4th Body mark) fits at 390x844 (buttons 722-762, dialog to 786). Headless Chromium hiding scrollbars is a harness quirk, but mobile browsers also use overlay scrollbars that stay hidden until the user scrolls, so the missing cue is real on phones. The formation papers' one long scroll is a low-priority wish (jump list or collapse) and was not re-measured; the papers staying a blocking dialog is accepted. DESIGN.md has no rule that keeps dialog actions in view, so this is a UX gap rather than a broken spec. The buttons can always be reached by scrolling inside the dialog, hence low.
verdicts.root_cause: frontend/src/components/pc/CircleView.jsx:244: the AdvancementModal dialog is one 'max-h-[90dvh] overflow-y-auto' box, and the Confirm/Later row (around line 449) is inside the scrolling body. frontend/src/components/pc/ScarModal.jsx:149 is the same pattern ('max-h-[calc(100dvh-32px)] overflow-y-auto'), with the Decide later / Record scar row at line 240 inside the scrolling body.
verdicts.fix: In both dialogs, make the panel 'flex flex-col' (keep the max-h). Wrap the content in a 'min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto' body, and move the action row out into a 'shrink-0' footer with the dialog's own background and a top rule, so the buttons stay pinned while the choices scroll. Optionally add one line under Later saying what it does ('You can pick them later from the Choose advancements button'). A jump list or collapse for the formation papers would be a separate product decision.
